process.title: Structure the problem, then test the decision in a real interface.
process.description: Each step produces something that can be reviewed. AI-assisted coding does not replace product reasoning.

steps.title: Find the real problem
steps.label: PROBLEM
steps.description: Start with a specific workflow, repeated task, or user complaint.

steps.title: Map the product flow
steps.label: FLOW
steps.description: Define inputs, system states, review points, outputs, and failure paths.

steps.title: Build a working prototype
steps.label: PROTOTYPE
steps.description: Use AI-assisted coding to test the flow in a real interface.

steps.title: Test it in use
steps.label: TEST
steps.description: Check the experience with realistic data, mobile interactions, and edge cases.

steps.title: Ship the result
steps.label: SHIP
steps.description: Add testing, documentation, deployment, and a stable way to try the product.

about.title1: Logic helps me structure the problem.
about.title2: Prototyping helps me test the product decision.
about.bio1: I’m Jamie Zhang, a graduate student in logic at China University of Political Science and Law. My academic training shapes how I separate assumptions, rules, reasoning, and conclusions—especially when designing AI-assisted products.
about.bio2: I apply that structure to product work: defining the problem, mapping the flow, shaping AI output, and building the interface with Next.js and TypeScript. I also handle testing, documentation, server deployment, and the final live experience.
about.opportunity: I’m currently looking for roles in AI product, product prototyping, and frontend product development.
